paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this passage. Jesus stands up on the biggest day of the feast and calls out in a loud voice, "If anyone is thirsty, let him come to Me and drink." (John 7:37) That's an invitation with no entrance exam. Whoever believes in Him, and "Streams of living water will flow from within him." (John 7:38)

The Gospel tells us He was speaking about the Spirit, whom those who believed in Him were later to receive (John 7:39). So this isn't a little sip you have to ration. It's the Spirit given to believers, and that is a whole lot more than a refill. Meanwhile the crowd argued over titles, and the officers walked back and said, "Never has anyone spoken like this man!" (John 7:46) I think those officers heard something you can't fake, friend.

Now look at who was fighting over Jesus and who was leaning toward Him. The rulers had their résumés, their Scripture arguments and their sure answers, and still turned Him away. Nicodemus stood in that room and asked about hearing a man before judging him (John 7:51), and I bet that took some NERVE. So here's the big idea: Jesus is still calling the thirsty, and the one who comes to Him and believes is the one who drinks. Don't let anybody's arguments about where He's from keep you from the cup, friend.
